newsitem.title: UAE: Electronic customs processing to boost efficiency.
newsitem.headline: Electronic customs processing to boost efficiency.

text.p: Global electronic customs processing is being considered to streamline customs operations and provide a more efficient service, a World Customs Organisation (WCO) official said on Monday.

"The concept of a worldwide electronic customs processing system is under active discussion and I have no doubt that this will, at least in part, become a reality during the next century," said Douglas Tweddle, director of customs procedures and enforcement at the WCO.

He said electronic communication between international traders and customs was part of a series of initiatives developed by the WCO together with the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) to facilitate international trade.
"(An) aspect of the ICC/WCO initiative is the development of a new era of electronic communication between international traders and customs," Tweddle said.
"The objective will be for information about particular international trade consignments to be made available by electronic means to all those who need and have the authority to access it," he said.
"This 'seamless data flow' or 'integrated data transaction'...could have a major impact on current customs procedures," Tweddle said.

The two-day cargo conference in Sharjah, which began on Sunday, is hosted by the Sharjah Airport Authority and organised by the Airports Council International, a world organisation for airports. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
